CHIEF COMPLAINT
Kidney stone with severe pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a female presenting with severe left-sided back pain that started approximately three days ago. She reports the pain is constant and has been traveling lower toward the groin. She denies passing the stone. She also reports hematuria noted this morning. Patient states she has had kidney stones twice before and typically passes them within three to four days. She notes today is approximately day three of this episode. She has tried acetaminophen and ibuprofen for pain relief without significant improvement. She reports some chills and mild nausea but denies fever. She is unable to eat due to pain and discomfort.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies chest pain and abdominal pain. She reports constant left flank pain radiating into the groin, chills, nausea, and hematuria. She is able to urinate.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Hypertension, Diabetes Mellitus Type 2, Recurrent kidney stones (third episode), Grade 2 out of 6 systolic ejection murmur (known, not currently concerning).

MEDICATIONS
Norvasc 2.5 mg for hypertension, Metformin 500 mg for diabetes, Acetaminophen as needed for pain, Ibuprofen as needed for pain.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient reports enjoying french fries and acknowledges difficulty limiting sodium intake.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Blood pressure elevated (likely due to pain). Heart: Grade 2 out of 6 systolic ejection murmur noted. Lungs: Clear bilaterally, no crackles or wheezes. Abdomen: Tenderness to palpation, no rebound or guarding. Costovertebral angle (CVA) tenderness on the right flank.

RESULTS
Not discussed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Kidney stone, third episode. Patient to receive Oxycodone 5 mg every 6 to 8 hours as needed for pain, continue acetaminophen for breakthrough pain, and increase fluid intake to help pass the stone. Patient will be provided with a urine strainer to collect stone if passed. Referral to Urology for evaluation and prevention of recurrent kidney stones. Hypertension: Continue Norvasc 2.5 mg, blood pressure readings acceptable. Diabetes: Continue Metformin 500 mg. Referral to Dietitian/Nutrition for dietary counseling and sodium restriction (goal 2300 mg/day). Patient counseled on importance of home blood pressure monitoring at least three times per week.
